craft_claim: Stylistic convergence toward the audience increases liking and rapport, but over-accommodation (simplifying or adapting beyond the audience's level) is perceived as patronizing.

supporting_evidence.location: Communication Accommodation Theory (Cambridge), ch. 3, pp. 36-59; origin Giles et al. 1973
supporting_evidence.note: Convergence reduces perceived differences from an interlocutor and is associated with liking, relational solidarity and communication satisfaction; the theory also models non-accommodation and over-accommodation.
Adapting speech beyond the optimal level (over-accommodation) is perceived as condescending and raises barriers rather than removing them.

counterevidence.note: Convergence can also be read as ingratiating or as threatening in-group boundaries, so it is not unconditionally positive.

scope: Audience calibration of register, diction and assumed knowledge; relevant to blog, copy, newsletter and instructional prose.
exceptions: Deliberate over-simplification for a genuinely novice audience may be appropriate if signalled and matched to real need.
